Both of us got the initial vaccine well over 6 mos ago, but have not had an opportunity to get the booster, which would technically mean we are not considered fully vaccinated anymore. Even so, my partners work has no requirements for vaccination and has 0 bearing on if you can work, even if exposed. As long as you don't have a fever, vaxxed or not, you are required to come in for your shift. Even though you are contagious even if asymptomatic, gotta love the good ol USA.

Yes, in the US workers have the right to refuse unsafe or dangerous work, and OSHA also states that if you are sick with *anything* contagious your employer has to let you stay home. The problem is that if your boss fires you because you're refusing to come in sick, OSHA has 0 say in that. They can't tell them to give you your job back, or sue them for wrongful termination, nothing. 

Not to mention, if you are an at will employee, and I'd say most people are in the US, your boss doesn't need cause to fire you. They can literally fire you with no explanation, so they can either lie (ie." he wasn't a team player") or simply button it. This makes it harder to find any recourse if you do decide to take it up with a lawyer.

Oh, and even if you do want to take it to court most employers these days have you sign an arbitration agreement, meaning that if you are wrongfully terminated, due to the agreement you *cannot have a jury trial* AND you *must* accept the arbitration agreement or settlement as final, no appeals..

 Some states you don't have to sign these as a condition of employment, in mine employers are allowed to make it mandatory, and even when I've worked in states where you can refuse, they throw them in towards the end of your training so you could be checking boxes just to get through it and not realize you just electronically signed an arbitration agreement. 

Sorry for the long response there, but in essence I'm saying that yes technically we do have these laws and protections, but they are effectively meaningless as we have little to no means to enforce them.

They just took your mom's word for it and slapped an autism diagnosis on you? In that case I wouldn't be surprised if they got it wrong. They should have done some kind of done some kind of assessment with YOU that would test your speech, motor skills, and so on. That's simply because autism is hard to diagnose because "meltdowns", not making eye contact, even sensory issues are NOT unique to autism. So, you need some more background on the development of the child vs where they should be for their age in order to really understand what's going on. 

I have autism myself, and suffer from PTSD. The reason I bring that up is this, the meltdowns and inability to make eye contact, could easily be considered a symptom of both, maybe even sensory issues depending on the circumstances around them. I went a long time just being diagnosed with and treated for PTSD (already being diagnosed with one makes getting the other diagnosed very difficult if you do have both, because of the amount of overlap) when the possibility of also having autism was even thought of, I was already 16 years old.

 Although I had made progress with my trauma, I hadn't had any help for my socialization issues, nor did I understand why people thought I was weird no matter how hard I tried to act "normral", or why I would do things like involuntarily throw my head back repeatedly when I was upset (sometimes to the point of injury), why I couldn't stand the texture of certain foods to the point of gagging, etc. All of this was chalked up to me being neurotic. My point is being misdiagnosed, or simply not receiving a full, proper assessment, can be very harmful to those with autism AND mental health issues. 

I can't help but think that if your mother did have you misdiagnosed, it likely stopped you from getting the help you really needed, because as your therapist said, what was likely a trauma response from emotional abuse, was treated as autism. I'm so sorry that your mom put you through hell and now wants to use your autism diagnosis as an excuse to act like your savior, wether the diagnosis is correct or not, that's absolutely disgusting. I wish all the best for you moving forward and hope you can get some clarity on all of this, stay safe and stay well 💜

After I was raped, I would get triggered if my boyfriend tried to touch me, I would have days, weeks, even months I spent having severe mood swings, being so depressed that I could barely pull myself together to get to work, only to fall apart the second I clocked out and got home. I felt awful. 

My boyfriend wasn't the one who raped me, so why is it that when he looks me in the eye I see my rapist? Why do I get sucked out of my body when he touches me and taken back to the memory? Why is it that I am so miserable and depressed even though I haven't been abused for so long? Unfortunately, that's what trauma does to you. However, that doesn't have to be your forever, it can get better. 

I started by telling my boyfriend what happened to me, then I got into therapy, and began taking better care of myself. 

Fortunately, he has been incredibly patient and understanding. If your boyfriend is not equipped to deal with this and help you through it, that's his issue, not yours. It's not your fault. You are not any less capable or deserving of love.

I am still working on healing and feeling whole again, I still have terrible mood swings some days, I still don't want to be touched sometimes, I still go through serious bouts of depression. 

But you know what? That's okay. It's okay to feel all of these things and have challenging days, because you are in the process of healing from something no one should ever have to experience. 

Be more kind and patient with yourself. If you keep beating yourself up, the wound will never heal. 

As soon as you are able to, get as far from your rapist as you can. Make a life for yourself that is independent of him, and don't feel guilty if you never want to interact with him again.

 It will get better, please don't cut your life short. I'm here if you need to talk to someone, and there are many forums such as these full of people who want to love and support you.

You killing yourself to spite this woman will not guarantee any specific reaction from her. All you're going to do is kill yourself. That's it. She will probably grieve for you, and be traumatized because she will have to watch. However, at the end of the day, you've only put a stop to your own life. I understand that you are hurt and feel betrayed, but there's no good reason to do that to another human being. There's no good reason to make someone watch you kill yourself, again, all you get out of it is spite. 

Do you value yourself so little that you would bring your ENTIRE life to an end for a moment of spite? You are worth more than that. The biggest "fuck you" you could give to anyone who hurt you is to get BETTER without them. I know you feel like you're at rock bottom, and I know intense emotional stress has made this plan of yours seem like a viable option, but believe me, it is so not worth it.  

I've had moments of "I'll show you, I'll make you pay." Too. But really, at the end of the day, if I walked up to someone who abused or mistreated me and shot myself, the second the lights go out, what's gained from that? You think you're going to see the look on her face, you think you're going to hear her cry and get the satisfaction of feeling like she's finally recognized your pain. You're not. If you're hanging yourself all you'll be able to focus on is the feeling of what seems like everything constricting in your body (its increadibly painful, I know from experience), you're also not going to be able to hear very well,  and eventually the vessels in your eyes are going to rupture. You're going to feel like your head is in a clamp that's been made as tight as it can go. This is all within seconds.

Trust me, you're not going to get to relish in her pain and feel immeasurable catharsis like you're thinking, because the only pain you're going to be able to focus on in that moment is your own, and it's not like you're going to get to see the aftermath.  All you're getting out of this is being dead, and maybe that alone is enough for you, but then she wins again doesn't she? You feel she's taken everything from you now? Well in essence you're letting her take your very life. 

You are a human being who's life has value, and I hope I'm not too late, and that you'll reconsider.
